extracted.intended_audience: principal investigators (PIs), signing officials (SOs), and institutional grant administrators preparing/submitting RPPRs and inclusion enrollment data via eRA Commons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, validating, and submitting Interim, Final, and annual Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) and associated Inclusion Enrollment Reports (IERs) and IRAMs via eRA Commons, including role-based permissions and system behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of eRA Commons RPPR module (AHRQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) grantees are required to use the eRA Commons RPPR module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AHRQ awardees must complete their progress reports using the RPPR module in eRA Commons; the RPPR references agency prior approval policies (see HHS Grants Policy Statement for AHRQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval required for significant changes in objectives/scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR includes numerous references to the NIH Grants Policy Statement, 8.1.2 requirement that significant changes in objectives and scope require prior approval of the agency; for AHRQ awardees the analogous requirement is in the HHS Grants Policy Statement under 'Prior Approval Requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed changes materially alter objectives or scope, contact your program official and obtain agency prior approval per the cited policy before implementing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: VA progress reporting timing and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports (RPPRs) are required to continue support of a VA-ORD award for each budget year within a competitive segment. Interim reports are due when the project period is over and the award is not in Closeout. If the pending renewal application is not funded, the Interim report becomes the Final report. Final reports are required for any funded award that has ended and will not be extended through renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA-ORD specific guidance for completing report content and submitting/ routing to VA-ORD is available at the VA RPPR resources link; note that VA outcomes are not published and some fields differ from NIH templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR availability window
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interim RPPR link will appear for both the principal investigator (PI) and the signing official (SO) one day after the budget period end date and before the award moves to Closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the Interim RPPR via Status search results; use the Initiate/Edit workflow described in Status to create and edit the Interim RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate vs Submit role restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the PI can initiate the RPPR, and only the SO can submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate the RPPR as PI (Initiate button). Editing can be done by users with appropriate access; only the institution's Signing Official may perform the final Submit to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRAM (Interim Report Additional Materials) requests and responders
rubrics_metrics.description: An awarding agency might issue the awardee a request for Interim Report Additional Materials (IRAM) following submission of an Interim RPPR. Either the PI or SO (or their delegates) can upload files and provide a revised project outcome in response to an IRAM request. For a multi-PI project, the contact PI can respond to the IRAM. However, only a SO can submit the IRAM package to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI/SO/delegates prepare response; only SO can perform final Submit; consult program official if unclear what to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRAM file upload limits and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare your response to the IRAM and save it in up to 10 PDF files that are each smaller than 6MB. The files you upload are instantly saved to eRA Commons system, but are not available to the agency until they are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files uploaded are saved locally in Commons; use Preview to download a combined summary and verify contents before SO submits. Remove files with the trash icon if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Outcome content, public posting, and character limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Project outcomes provide information regarding the cumulative outcomes or findings of the project. Note that outcomes are made available to the general public once approved by the program official, allowing recipients to provide a concise summary of the cumulative outcomes or findings of the project at the end of a competitive segment. For NIH awards the length of the outcome statement should not exceed 2000 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes must be written for the general public in clear, concise, and comprehensible language; suitable for electronic dissemination; and must not include proprietary, confidential information or trade secrets. Samples of acceptable project outcomes are provided at the NIH sample outcomes link.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRAM screen actions (Save, Preview, Delete, Submit) and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: On the IRAM screen you can upload files, enter a revised outcome (up to 2000 characters), Save, Preview (downloads summary + files), Delete the submission package, and Submit the IRAM package to the awarding agency. Only SOs have a Submit button; PIs cannot submit IRAM to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Save to retain text and files. Preview produces a downloadable package to review before submission. SO must perform final Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR required timing (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) is required for any grant that has ended and any grant that is not to be extended through award of a new competitive segment. The report is due within 120 days of the end of the project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the Final RPPR per awarding component instructions and submit via the Closeout Status screen using the Process Final RPPR button; follow PI/SO role rules for initiation and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR requirement when renewal submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient organization has submitted a renewal application on or before the date by which a Final RPPR would be required for the current competitive segment, then submission of an Interim RPPR via eRA Commons is required. The Interim RPPR will be used for the submission of a Competing Renewal application (Type 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim RPPR must be submitted within 120 days of the project end date. If the renewal is awarded the Interim RPPR will be treated as your annual RPPR; if not, the Interim RPPR will be accepted as the Final RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim/Final RPPR content differences vs annual RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences between Interim/Final RPPR and the annual RPPR are: In the Interim/Final RPPR, only D.1 is required in the Participants section; Sections F: Changes and Section H: Budget are not part of the Interim/Final RPPR; Section I: Outcomes is required for both the Interim/Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The format of Interim, Final, and annual RPPR are otherwise the same, so navigation and completion are similar; ensure omitted sections (F and H) are not expected for Interim/Final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-by-field guidance reference for Sections A–I
rubrics_metrics.description: Field-by-field guidance is available for completing the NIH, AHRQ, and VA Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs). Refer to the NIH and Other PHS Agency RPPR Instruction Guide for completing Sections A–I of the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cited Instruction Guide for detailed instructions on completing each RPPR section; note the guide does not apply to Department of Commerce (DOC) awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save before accessing Human Subjects System (HSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPORTANT: Before clicking the Human Subjects link, click the Save button on the RPPR to save all your work in Section G. Failure to do so will result in a loss of data on your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always save RPPR edits before following links that open other modules (HSS) to avoid data loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning for accessing HSS >60 days before due date
rubrics_metrics.description: If you click the Human Subjects more than 60 days before the progress report due date, the following warning is displayed: 'Based on the due date of this RPPR, inclusion data is not yet needed. If you proceed, access to the inclusion data via Commons/Status will be blocked. You cannot undo this action. Are you sure you want to proceed?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeding will block editing via Commons/Status (view only) until RPPR submission; consider whether editing now is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT) population for Forms E
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPORTANT: If the initial competitive segment was submitted on or after January 25, 2018 (i.e. a Forms E application) without a ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier (an NCT number), enter the appropriate NCT number in the field numbered 1.5. Click the Populate button and the system will do a best effort copy of form data from the official Clinical Trials records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the NCT number to enable auto-population of clinical trial information into the study record.

rubrics_metrics.name: IER data collection structure and optional fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Standalone PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report forms are no longer used. Instead, data collection for up to 20 Inclusion Enrollment Reports has been folded into each Study Record. For each IER, applicants will need to indicate whether an existing dataset or resource will be used and whether the enrollment location type is domestic or foreign. There are also a few optional fields in the report, including a text entry Comments section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Study Record screen to initiate and manage up to 20 IERs per study; provide dataset/resource and domestic/foreign indicators and optional comments as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing inclusion counts: two methods and template requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways to edit the existing Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) data for Cumulative (Actual) counts: (1) update the cells online in the existing report itself; (2) download a template for entering participant-level data (CSV), fill it out, and upload it which will populate the cells in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uploading, you must use the provided CSV template (Download Participant Level Data Template). You can download current participant-level data for records, or Remove Current Participant Level Data to clear records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned counts update rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Planned counts, the cells must be updated online in the report itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned enrollment cannot be updated via the participant-level CSV upload; edit planned fields directly in the IER online form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual-level participant data requirement (effective dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual-level participant data on characteristics at enrollment will be required in-progress reports for competitive applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2019 (See NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-18-116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your templates and processes collect participant-level characteristics for applicable submissions; follow the cited guide notice for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI and SO locking and submission workflows for study edits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PI is making changes: The PI can click the Save and Release Lock button to save the changes; the submission status changes to Work in Progress; PI changes status to Ready for Submission; SO logs into ASSIST, finds the application, and submits it. If the SO is making changes: The SO can click the Save and Keep Lock button to save the changes; the submission status remains in Work in Progress; the SO must click the Save and Release Lock button to allow the application to have the status changed; SO changes status to Ready for Submission; the Submit action becomes active and SO clicks Submit. Only the SO can submit the application to NIH. The submission sends all updated study records associated with the application to NIH at one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Save/Lock conventions appropriate to the user role to coordinate edits between PI and SO; program officials and grant specialists are notified automatically of study changes; some changes may require prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to planned enrollment require contacting program officer
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are changes from the planned enrollment originally approved for funding, contact the program officer to discuss updating/revising the planned enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section G – Special Reporting Requirements of the RPPR Instruction Guide for further instructions and any required prior approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert delayed onset study to full study record
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is time to activate a delayed onset study, access the study record through Status and use the Convert action to change the status to a full study. Clicking 'Convert' will change this record to a full study record and the study will no longer be considered delayed onset. The delayed onset justification will be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Convert, complete fields on the Study Page and Save (keep or release lock). Saving removes the study from the Delayed Onset table and adds a new study in the Study Record table. Cancel will retain delayed onset status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Record (IER) status values and meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: A status will be maintained for each study version. IER Status values include: Accepted – Not Rolled Forward; Accepted (Original Submission); Accepted (PI Revisions); Accepted by Agency; Grantee Updates in Progress; Inclusion Updated; Previous FY Data; Pending SO; Received by Agency; Received by Agency – RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each status has a specific meaning (e.g., 'Grantee Updates in Progress' indicates the grantee initiated updates; 'Received by Agency – RPPR' indicates IER submitted as part of RPPR). Use the statuses to track IER lifecycle and routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to access HSS via Status versus RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: HSS is used to view and maintain inclusion data associated with your grant(s) and can be accessed via the Status module or via RPPR Section G. Use Status when: before award of a competitive application changes may be necessary; post-award there may be a requirement to provide more frequent updates in addition to RPPR reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion data cannot always be updated using Status (e.g., under peer review). After award, data for a fiscal year is locked; updates via Status apply to the next fiscal year's record. Refer to Access HSS and HSS Online Help for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Inclusion Enrollment Records provided — RPPR submission block
rubrics_metrics.description: When inclusion monitoring is required and no inclusion enrollment records (IERs) exist, the RPPR system will not allow the submission of the progress report without an IER. An error message will be displayed when you check errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system will display the specific error directing you to G.4.b of the RPPR to update the study and provide an IER. Address missing IERs before attempting submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning messages for missing or stale inclusion data
rubrics_metrics.description: Warnings display when additional data is expected or when actuals have not been updated in over one year (365 days). Examples: 'No Cumulative inclusion enrollment data has been provided...' and 'Updates to Inclusion enrollment report(s) have not been made for study#<study#>. If updates are needed, navigate to G.4.b...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enrollment has not begun you may proceed; otherwise update cumulative counts. Regularly update IERs to avoid warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for Errors functionality and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time before an RPPR is submitted to agency, an error check can be performed to verify that the report passes the business rules and system validations in place. Errors and warnings that are reported are underlined and linked. There are two ways to check for errors: Check for errors on the current form (button at bottom of form) and Check for errors on all forms at once (three-dot ellipsis menu on RPPR Menu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed errors are clickable and must be corrected prior to submission; the system will prevent submission of an RPPR containing errors. Warnings do not prevent submission. If all validations pass, 'No errors found on validation' displays. For multi-project RPPRs, validation can be run per overall or per component.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF upload format recommendation (flattened PDFs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOTE: All PDFs you upload are recommended to be a flattened PDF, and may cause an error if not flattened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you receive errors about flattening PDFs, consult the FAQ 'When submitting PDFs to eRA Commons... ensure all files are flattened PDFs' for instructions on how to flatten PDF files before upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error/warning display conventions in multi-project RPPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: If errors or a warning exist for the chosen component, the appropriate error or warning message displays for each failed occurrence. Listed errors, which are clickable, must be corrected prior to submission; the system will prevent submission of an RPPR containing errors. Warnings are in yellow; errors are in red/pink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the component-level check for errors on multi-project RPPRs and address errors in each component before submission.
